title: automated postgres quorum-shift playbooks + terraform VIP shift
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds automated quorum-shift tooling for on-prem Postgres clusters: Terraform VIP shift module, Ansible orchestrator playbook, Helm operator tweaks, runbooks-as-code, and end-to-end validation tests. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind installer flag.
description: Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ/on-prem topologies reported long manual windows when performing Postgres primary failovers across AZs (VIP moves, datastore fencing, and cache sync). This PR implements an opinionated, automatable quorum-shift workflow that can be invoked as part of DR drills and automated failovers. The goal is to reduce manual steps, provide safe rollbacks, and validate restores as code. High level: 1) Terraform module to atomically shift a virtual IP (VIP) and update firewall routes; 2) Ansible orchestrator playbook that coordinates operator actions (promote, demote, drain), runs pre/post checks, applies fencing if needed, and calls the Terraform VIP shift as a sub-step; 3) Helm chart updates to the postgres-operator that expose safe promotion hooks and a readiness probe to detect in-flight replication lag; 4) Runbooks-as-code (Markdown) that codify the drill steps and include automated checklists; 5) A restore-validation script and E2E test to exercise snapshot restore after quorum shift. Implementation notes: - Everything is feature-gated behind installer flag 'enable_dr_quorum_shift' to avoid changing behavior for existing installs. - Terraform module placed under terraform/modules/vip-shift with support for multiple providers (MetalLB, Keepalived). - Ansible playbook ansible/playbooks/quorum_shift.yml is idempotent and includes --check dry-run support as well as interactive mode. - Helm updates in helm/charts/postgres-operator/ add two new hooks: pre-promote and post-demote along with configurable wait timeouts. - docs/runbooks/dr_quorum_shift.md contains step-by-step, expected outcomes, mitigation steps, and automated rollback snippet. Testing: local unit tests for the Terraform module with terratest wrappers, Ansible linting and molecule scenarios (mocked), CI E2E that runs a simulated cluster using kind + containerized Postgres operator and invokes the playbook followed by restore-validation.sh. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + docs - [x] Ansible orchestrator playbook - [x] Helm operator hooks + values - [x] Runbooks-as-code - [x] E2E validation test - [x] CI workflow to run the drill in sandbox Security considerations: the Terraform module requires change control for VIPs; the playbook enforces least-privilege service accounts when interacting with K8s APIs. Rollback strategy: the orchestrator supports an automatic rollback path (reverse steps) if post-checks fail; there is also a manual rollback section in the runbook that documents how to reassign VIP and re-declare the previous primary. Linear/Jira: related to ENG-5312, SRE-402, and SUP-1187. Links: internal runbook: docs/runbooks/dr_quorum_shift.md.

review_comments: Jordan Reyes: Overall looks solid. Two asks: (1) increase default promotion timeout to 5m to avoid flaky CI; (2) add explicit CRD readiness check before demotion. Please address and request another review.
Maya Chen: Thanks — bumped default to 5m and added CRD readiness check in ansible tasks. Also added a note about controlling pod disruption budgets in the runbook.

Priya Nair: CI flake observed on first run: terraform provider timeout when provider returned 409 on VIP create. Recommend adding retry with exponential backoff in module. Also confirm provider compatibility with Keepalived vs MetalLB.
Maya Chen: Added retry wrapper around provider calls and documented provider compatibility matrix in terraform/modules/vip-shift/README.md. CI re-run requested.
CI Bot: initial run failed (terraform apply timeout). Rerun triggered by @Maya Chen.
CI Bot: subsequent run succeeded (all checks green).
Tom Becker: Approved after verifying e2e passes in sandbox and reading runbook. +1 for runbooks-as-code format.
ci_log_summary: Initial pipeline failed on terraform apply timeout. Fixed by adding provider retries and increasing timeouts. Subsequent pipeline run passed all lint, unit tests, molecule, and e2e validations.
testing_notes: Local verification: molecule scenario 'dr_orchestrator' passed against containerized Postgres nodes. Terratest wrapper validates VIP shift for MetalLB and Keepalived providers. E2E run in CI exercised full converge -> promote -> VIP shift -> post-checks -> snapshot -> restore -> restore-validation.sh.
manual_merge_notes: Merged via squash merge after sign-off from SRE and infra leads. No database schema changes; low risk but recommend scheduling non-business hours for initial rollout on customer clusters.

notes_for_ops: Feature is disabled by default. To enable set installer flag 'enable_dr_quorum_shift: true' and review terraform provider credentials. Run the included ansible playbook with --check for a dry-run. Ensure snapshots are available before promoting primary.
egress_restrictions: None added by this PR; terraform uses existing provider patterns and ansible uses installer-managed service accounts.
changelog_entry: Added DR orchestration: automated Postgres quorum shift (Terraform VIP shift, Ansible orchestrator, Helm operator hooks, runbooks-as-code, e2e validation).
